title: Prioritizing demand-side use of clean hydrogen for cost-effective mitigation
abstract: Clean hydrogen is widely proposed for hard-to-abate sector decarbonization, but its limited supply requires prioritizing sectors with the highest value. This study evaluates ten sectors and identifies key no-regret uses, while highlighting the need for specific demand-side policies.

title: Inherited lithospheric weakness enabled rapid stress transmission across Tibet
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K–Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India–Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict.

title: Mechanistic insights into NET1–UNC5B complex formation and Its targeted disruption by NP137 fab and NET1 peptide competitors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Netrin‑1, a secreted protein initially characterized for its role in axon guidance, has emerged as a critical mediator of cancer progression. Preclinical studies with the anti‑netrin‑1 antibody NP137, which blocks the netrin‑1–UNC5B interaction, have demonstrated reactivation of tumor suppressor functions and sensitization of cancer cells to chemotherapy. Here, we identified the molecular binding interface of the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex using integrative structural and quantitative biophysical analyses. We then determined how NP137 binding inhibits this interaction by sterically blocking key contact points within the interface. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we rationally designed peptides that disrupt the netrin‑1–UNC5B complex through interfering with heparin-mediated stabilization of the complex by binding to shared heparin-binding sites. This comprehensive structural and mechanistic analysis advances understanding of netrin‑1 signaling and establishes strategies for therapeutic intervention in netrin‑1-driven malignancies.

title: Myosin filaments of vertebrate skeletal and cardiac muscle are highly similar, but not identical
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Striated muscles consist of two filament types, one based on actin, one based on myosin. All striated muscle actin filaments are highly similar. Invertebrate myosin filaments are heterogeneous; those of vertebrates are homogeneous. Mouse and human cardiac muscle myosin filaments are highly similar. How similar are they to those of skeletal muscle? Using Mavacamten for myosin head stabilization, we find the relaxed thick filaments of rabbit skeletal, human cardiac and mouse cardiac muscles are highly similar, differing primarily in the positioning of myosin binding protein C domains, C5-C7. In isolated cardiac thick filaments, C5-C7 lie along the filament backbone. In mouse and human cardiac myofibrils, C7 extends radially toward the thin filament. Here we show in isolated rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments, C7 also extends outward but with C6 bending azimuthally to position C5 onto titin suggesting a thick filament architecture highly adaptable to multiple functions with relatively simple structural changes.

title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10−25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10−20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10−09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells.

title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: UHRF1 is a chromatin-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryos. Uhrf1⁻/⁻ ESCs exhibited near-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1-null embryos developed normally until E8.5 and then failed to develop further by E9.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss. Single-cell multi-omic (ME-seq) profiling of E8.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis-regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP-related ligand–receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis.

title: Frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid renewable P2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H) enables large-scale renewable energy utilization and supports the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors, such as chemicals and maritime transport, via hydrogen-based renewable ammonia and methanol fuels. As a result, utility-scale ReP2H projects are expanding worldwide. However, off-grid ReP2H systems exhibit low inertia due to their converter-dominated nature, making frequency security a critical concern. Although recent studies show that electrolyzers can contribute to frequency regulation (FR), their support capability depends on operating states and loading levels, creating a trade-off between hydrogen output and frequency security. To address this challenge, this work develops a unified co-optimization framework for frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid ReP2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers. A system-level frequency response model is established to capture multi-stage FR from alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs), proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMELs), and other resources, including ammonia-fueled generators retrofitted in co-located chemical plants, battery energy storage, and wind turbines (WTs). Stage-wise transient frequency security constraints are derived, reformulated into tractable forms, and embedded into production scheduling, enabling coordinated on/off switching and load allocation across electrolyzers to maximize hydrogen output under uncertain renewable power input while enforcing frequency security constraints. Case studies based on real-world systems demonstrate that the proposed approach allows hydrogen plants to replace 55.52% and 96.85% of FR reserves from WTs and AFGs, respectively, while improving the system-level net hydrogen yield by substantially reducing ammonia-fuel consumption. Year-long simulations show an average 28.96% increase in annual net profit resulting from reduced reliance on conventional reserves.

title: A probability-box framework for quantifying office building air conditioning flexibility under multi-source uncertainty
abstract: Air conditioning systems are important flexible resources in buildings. However, their flexibility potential is highly uncertain due to unpredictable load disturbances caused by weather and occupancy variations. These uncertainties often lead to inconsistent load reduction outcomes, even when identical operating strategies are applied. To address the challenge of accurate quantification, this study proposes a probability box (P-box) model to characterize such potential under uncertainty. After defining the perturbation ranges and probability distributions of uncertain parameters, a stochastic load scenario generation method is employed, combining Monte Carlo sampling with Savitzky-Golay filtering to simulate multi-source disturbance conditions. The proposed P-box model is then evaluated for its prediction accuracy and adaptability based on these scenarios. The method is demonstrated using a calibrated office-building model in Tianjin under summer cooling conditions. Results show that under temperature reset and precooling strategies, the P-box model yields remarkably low prediction errors, the Wasserstein-based prediction achieves relative errors of 9.22% and 4.58% with respect to load reduction simulated under field-measured inputs, compared with 16.98% and 7.90% for the traditional deterministic methods. Moreover, the 100% P-box interval enveloped all evaluated samples, while narrower confidence intervals provided risk-dependent coverage, which accurately delineates the adjustable load range of buildings under multi-source disturbance conditions. This provides a reliable representation method for flexible resource scheduling and demand response strategy formulation.

title: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pangolins harbor SARS-CoV-2–related coronaviruses (PCoVs). We isolate three PCoVs (P8V, P11V, P5V) from confiscated Malayan pangolins and analyzed their genomes, evolution and functional properties. Phylogenetic analyses place these viruses in two clusters within the PCoV-GX lineage, revealing spike mutations that later convergently evolve in SARS-CoV-2. All viruses replicate efficiently in Vero E6 cells, with variable replication in human cell lines and organoids. In hACE2-transgenic mice, P11V and previously isolated P2V cause rapid, severe disease, whereas P8V and P5V exhibit delayed pathogenicity. Direct-contact transmission in hamsters is efficient for all strains, with lung pathology reflecting strain-specific virulence. These results demonstrate that PCoVs possess substantial infectivity, pathogenicity, and transmissibility, illustrating their adaptability, and highlight the role of pangolins as reservoirs of coronaviruses with zoonotic potential.

title: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy poses challenges in Mendelian randomization (MR) by biasing causal estimates, particularly when using numerous instrumental variables (IVs). We propose MRZ, a method that leverages IV-outcome association z-scores modeled as a mixture distribution to distinguish causal effects from IV-specific pleiotropy. MRZ classifies IVs into three categories: valid, uncorrelated pleiotropic, or correlated pleiotropic, enabling simultaneous estimation of causal and pleiotropic parameters through likelihood-based inference. Simulations demonstrate MRZ’s superior robustness and accuracy across diverse pleiotropic scenarios. When applied to investigate appendicular lean mass (ALM) and lipid traits, MRZ identifies significant negative causal effects of ALM on total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), with no evidence of reverse causation. In contrast, existing methods frequently suggest bidirectional effects. Randomized controlled experiments in mice validate MRZ results, confirming ALM’s causal effects on TC/LDL-C but not vice versa. By addressing key limitations of conventional approaches vulnerable to horizontal pleiotropy, MRZ advances causal inference in complex trait architectures.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk.

title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. Recent work reported that chromosomal gene position determines mRNA localization within Escherichia coli cells, implying a widespread genome-guided organizing mechanism. Yet this interpretation contrasts with biophysical expectations based on translation and diffusion and may be confounded by nascent transcription. Here, we examine this phenomenon by analyzing intracellular spatial transcriptomics datasets spanning different methods, bacterial species, growth conditions, and thousands of genes. We confirm the presence of genome-associated localization signatures that track chromosome macrodomain dynamics across the cell cycle and establish causality by repositioning a gene at distinct chromosomal loci. Quantitative analysis, however, shows that these signatures generally involve only a minority of transcripts and are of magnitudes consistent with reported rates of nascent transcription. Moreover, genome-associated patterns preferentially occur in weakly translated and unstable mRNAs. Together, our results indicate that genome-guided localization is unlikely to be a dominant driver of transcript positioning in bacteria.

title: Operando resolution of CO2 electrolysis interfaces at application-relevant current density reveals water gating
abstract: Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. Here operando Raman spectroscopy is used in combination with molecular dynamics simulations to establish the role of water ordering in the mechanism of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction over a range of current densities and under practical conditions.

title: High wind speed reduces water use efficiency across terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: The role of wind in ecosystem water use efficiency remains unclear. The authors show that water use efficiency declines with increasing wind speed, driven mainly by increases in evapotranspiration and secondarily by reductions in gross primary productivity.

title: Warming-driven lower-tropospheric stratification intensifies ducting over global oceans
abstract: Atmospheric ducts are waveguides that affect electromagnetic propagation in the atmosphere, affecting radar and other technologies. Here the authors show that warming intensifies such ducting over mid- to low-latitude oceans.

title: Warming oceans hit the battlefield
abstract: Marine radar signal propagation is highly sensitive to fine-scale vertical changes in water vapour. Now research shows that long-term increases in sea surface temperatures are strengthening the frequency and intensity of the features that allow radar signals to travel further than expected.

title: Combining climate policy instruments for a just transition to a climate-neutral economy
abstract: A distributional analysis of European Union climate policy pathways traces the costs of reducing carbon dioxide emissions to the level of households based on their spending and income patterns. We find that different equity considerations, including income inequality and within-group impact divergence, can shape optimal climate policy design with carbon prices, transfers, standards and subsidies.

title: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) – a key cytokine upregulated during MIA – perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Macrophage pyroptosis has been identified as a contributor to acute kidney injury (AKI), but the underlying mechanisms involved remain unclear. Herein, we identify that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) RNF130 is significantly downregulated in both mice and patients with AKI. Myeloid cell-specific loss of RNF130 aggravates renal pathological damage and facilitates macrophage pyroptosis in AKI mouse models. Proteomics analyses and experimental validation show that RNF130 deficiency prevents the ubiquitination of programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) dependent on the lysine 402 of PDCD4. Activated PDCD4 promotes the phosphorylation of NF-κB and STAT3, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-1-mediated cleavage of GSDMD, contributing to macrophage pyroptosis. Overexpression of PDCD4 nullifies the beneficial role of RNF130. High-throughput screening of a compound library identified that Nystose effectively mitigated renal injury in ischemic AKI mice by targeting and upregulating RNF130. These findings highlight the potential of RNF130 as a promising target for AKI.

title: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Malawi polyomavirus (MWPyV) has been detected in respiratory and gastrointestinal specimens, mostly in children; however there are limited data on its distribution and diversity. Here, we analyse n = 233 oropharyngeal swabs, collected from pediatric patients in São Paulo State, Brazil for MWPyV and potential co-infections using an integrated molecular, phylogenetic, and ultrastructural approach. We detect MWPyV DNA in 18 samples (7.7%) with low viral loads (mean 266 copies/reaction; range 13-2.3 × 103). Our phylogenetic analysis assigns six genomic sequences to genotype I and one to genotype III. The genome of genotype III shows evidence of putative recombination events with genomic regions related to genotypes II and III. One genotype I sequence forms a distinct phylogenetic branch, suggesting an unsampled or transitional lineage. Our findings provide evidence into the genomic diversity, viral recombination and potentially diverging lineages of MWPyV in pediatric patients.

title: Ammonium Ion Intercalation Enabled Stable 1T-VS2/WS2-Nb2CTx Heterostructures during Electrochemical Charge Storage
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.

title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

title: Fast, Hybrid Perovskite Deposition via Gas Flow Assisted Single Source Flash Evaporation
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.0) triggered major subaqueous delta collapses, generating massive tsunamis with maximum run-ups of ~50 m and ~13 m, respectively. Historical accounts from the Vatican Library and archeological evidence support these reconstructions. Since the last collapse, eight centuries of human-induced erosion have rebuilt the delta, leaving shoreline populations highly vulnerable to future earthquake-triggered failures. A global lake synthesis showed that human-driven erosion has reached its highest levels since the Industrial Era, progressively overloading deltas worldwide; thus, similar catastrophic failures may become more likely in the future. These findings reveal a persistent, human-amplified mechanism of lacustrine tsunami generation and intensity with major implications for hazard assessment.

title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program.

title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.

title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA, previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

title: Self-regenerating photocatalytic water treatment systems: integrating cognitive AI control, bio-inspired self-healing, and thermoelectric energy harvesting
abstract: Conventional photocatalytic water treatment systems face persistent limitations in terms of catalyst deactivation, energy consumption, and adaptability to variable influent quality. This review examines the integration of three emerging technological domains, machine learning driven process optimization, bio-inspired self-healing material strategies, and thermoelectric energy recovery, as a framework for developing more autonomous and resource-efficient photocatalytic treatment systems. A systematic literature search was conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed (January 2001 to June 2024), following PRISMA guidelines. After multi-step screening, 104 peer-reviewed studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. Reviewed studies reported degradation efficiencies above 85% for model recalcitrant pollutants under optimized conditions. ML approaches, particularly artificial neural networks and ensemble methods, improved predictive accuracy of degradation kinetics by 20–35% relative to empirical models. Self-healing polymeric matrices retained catalytic activity exceeding 80% after repeated use cycles. Thermoelectric modules integrated in solar-driven reactors generated partial energy offsets under laboratory conditions, though full energy self-sufficiency has not yet been demonstrated at the pilot scale. Critical challenges remain, including long-term material stability under real wastewater conditions, scalability of digital twin architectures, and rigorous techno-economic validation. A research roadmap to address these barriers is proposed, with an emphasis on pilot-scale demonstration and standardized performance benchmarking.

title: Interlayer sliding controls magnetism in tetralayer graphene
abstract: The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. This sliding transition now enables ferromagnetic states present only in the rhombohedral stacking to be turned on and off through structural control.

title: Your battery may not be a battery
abstract: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.

title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

title: Coupling hfCas13d with Circular gRNA Array Precursors Extends RNA Knockdown and Improves Biocatalysis in Yeast
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: CRISPR-based RNA cleavage holds promise for gene knockdown but its applications in metabolic engineering remain largely unexplored. Here we reconstitute three mammalian CRISPR-based RNA cleavage systems to arrest the intermediate metabolic reactions in the yeast Candida viswanathii to produce hydroxydecanoic acid (HDA), an important nylon precursor. We identify hfCas13d as the optimal effector and next develop a circular guide RNA (CgRNA) precursor architecture to enhance and extend the knockdown of genes involved in HDA production. This hfCas13d/CgRNA precursor platform also represses genes in other yeasts and E. coli, demonstrating broad microbial applicability. Single and dual CgRNA precursor arrays enable multiplexed pathway repression, with dual arrays reducing byproduct formation and increasing HDA titer to 17.8 g/L in shake flasks. Bioreactor fermentation further boosts HDA production to 37.2 g/L. Together, this work establishes hfCas13d/CgRNA as a programmable RNA regulatory platform for engineering microbial cell factories.

title: Rotation‐Coupled Guest Anions Stabilize Polymer Solid‐State Sodium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries are constrained by sluggish Na + migration and unstable sodium–metal interfaces, both of which are closely associated with poorly regulated solvation chemistry. Here we report a rotation‐coupled guest‐anion strategy in a poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene)‐based solid‐state electrolyte (PHSE) using Mg(OTf) 2 . Mg 2+ preferentially coordinates DMF and TFSI − , weakening Na + –TFSI − association and limiting solvent‐derived reactions at the sodium metal anode. OTf − enters the Na + solvation shell as a mobile guest anion. Its C─S rotational axis and equivalent oxygen coordination sites allow conformational rotation to synchronize with Na + hopping along polymer chains. This anchor–rotator chemistry reorganizes Na + coordination, lowers the migration barrier, and promotes an inorganic‐rich, Mg─O‐containing interphase. The optimized electrolyte enables Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 ||Na cells to retain 94.2% capacity after 1100 cycles at 2C and supports a 94 mAh pouch cell with stable cycling. It also enables high‐voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 O 2 F||Na cells to retain 93.6% capacity after 1000 cycles at 0.5C over 2.5–4.2 V. Comparative evaluation across a total of 20 polymer electrolyte systems with varied polymer matrices and anion structures identifies anion symmetry, rotational periodicity, and finite rotational barriers as molecular criteria for designing stable polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries.

title: Efficient Bipolar Hydrogen Peroxide Production Through Photoelectrochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. Photoanodes in bias‐free photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems suffer from poor H 2 O 2 selectivity at low potentials, limiting the efficiency of bipolar H 2 O 2 production. Herein, we report a rare‐earth ytterbium oxide (YbO x ) modified BiVO 4 /WO 3 photoanode for efficient PEC water oxidation to H 2 O 2 . The optimized photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 4.83 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE , an H 2 O 2 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of over 80% across the potential range of 0.6–1.8 V RHE , and a peak FE of 90.4% at 1.6 V RHE . Yb 3+ Lewis acid sites suppress the competitive four‐electron oxygen evolution reaction by forming Yb‐hydroxyl complexes, while YbO x enhances charge transfer and reduces interfacial resistance. Importantly, when coupled with a FeZnWMnYb high‐entropy amorphous oxide cathode for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction, the bias‐free tandem cell achieves ∼160% bipolar H 2 O 2 FE. Scaling the photoelectrode to 20 cm 2 under 0.7 suns illumination yields an H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.03 mmol L −1 h −1 . This work demonstrates a viable strategy for large‐scale solar‐driven H 2 O 2 synthesis for environmental applications.

title: Radical‐Mediated Surface Reconstruction of SnO 2 Nanocrystals Enables Efficient and Durable Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Charge‐transport layers fundamentally dictate interfacial recombination, carrier extraction, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet scalable routes to simultaneously regulate their colloidal stability and defect chemistry remain elusive. Here, we report a radical‐mediated surface reconstruction strategy for ligand‐free SnO 2 nanocrystals that enables concurrent gains in device efficiency, scalability, and durability. Sonochemical activation generates hydroxyl radicals that selectively passivate oxygen‐deficient Sn sites while inducing electrostatically stabilized dispersions with exceptional shelf stability, allowing the SnO 2 colloids to be stored for over 2 years without aggregation or performance degradation. This stabilization enables the formation of uniform electron transport layers with reduced trap density and enhanced electron mobility. These improvements promote buried‐interface perovskite crystallization and accelerate charge extraction, yielding PSCs with an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 26.12%). Importantly, the strategy is inherently scalable, enabling a perovskite module (∼110 cm 2 ) with an efficiency of 21.45%. Devices exhibit enhanced operational stability, retaining 92% efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2), maintaining 88% efficiency under maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and showing negligible degradation over 500 thermal cycles (ISOS‐T‐3). These results establish radical‐mediated engineering of SnO 2 nanocrystals as a general pathway in perovskite photovoltaics, bridging high efficiency, large‐area manufacturability, and long‐term operational stability.

title: Chiralizing Covalent Organic Frameworks to Boost H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven H 2 O 2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on‐site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O 2 to spin‐paired H 2 O 2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active‐site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O 2 . Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H 2 O 2 , and report a chiralization strategy for spin‐regulated H 2 O 2 photosynthesis in β‐ketoenamine‐linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin‐selective electron transport, favor the O–O‐bond‐preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H 2 O 2 formation. Chiralization enhances H 2 O 2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine‐containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g −1 h −1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial‐agent‐free COF systems. Membrane‐integrated chiral COFs enable continuous‐flow H 2 O 2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin‐selective electron transport with O 2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.

title: Synthesis of gem ‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
abstract: ABSTRACT The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. Herein, we disclose a palladium‐catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C(sp 2 )─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si‐ and P‐stereocenters. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon‐stereogenic gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P‐stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 er). Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: “Direct Injection” Bubble Growth Mediated by Nano‐Interfaced Electrodes for Efficient Chlorine Production
abstract: ABSTRACT The chlor‐alkali industry, with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) as its core anodic process, accounts for nearly 4% of global electricity consumption. The development of energy‐efficient and stable CER system is therefore urgently needed. Nano‐interfaced electrodes exhibit superior catalytic performance, yet their mechanism for energy saving and system stability remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine a high‐speed camera and confocal laser scanning microscope Platform to visualize and digitalize the bubble evolution and the bubble‐induced overpotential ( ƞ bub ). We provide direct visual evidence that the bubble‐induced concentration gradients and fluid flow field disturbances are key regulators of overpotential, and that the nano‐interfaced electrode exhibits an ƞ bub of only approximately 49% of that of the flat‐interfaced electrode. Specifically, the nano interface not only generates a stronger interfacial electric field and enhanced bubble‐induced interfacial turbulence—which promote the Cl − migration to the electrode surface—but also induces a “direct‐injection” mode of bubble growth that mitigates the accumulation of reaction products near the electrode. Moreover, the Cl − enrichment capacity of the nano interface endows the near‐interface solution with ionic buffering capability, effectively suppressing potential fluctuations. This work demonstrates that regulating bubble dynamics is key to constructing energy‐saving and stable gas‐evolving electrochemical systems.

title: Crystallography‐Dependent Plating/Stripping Kinetics and Interfacial Morphologies in Zn Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Crystallographic orientation governs Zn deposition, dissolution, and cycling stability, but its influence on interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics remains difficult to quantify. Here, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy coupled with fast scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) is used to resolve Zn plating and stripping on single‐crystal (002), (100), and (101) surfaces. Meniscus‐confined measurements reveal facet‐dependent branch‐specific apparent zero‐current potentials and apparent exchange current densities, j 0 , with the kinetic ordering j 0 (100) > j 0 (101) > j 0 (002) for both plating and stripping. This ordering is reproduced across independently prepared electrodes and retained over different scan rates and aqueous electrolytes. Beyond charge transfer, Zn removal and regrowth are strongly crystallographically encoded: dissolution footprints preserve the symmetry of the parent facets, while potentiostatically deposited Zn adopts substrate‐dependent growth geometries. These coupled kinetic and morphological differences translate directly to battery performance. Despite its slower apparent kinetics, the close‐packed, low‐energy (002) facet exhibits the longest cycling life in Zn/Zn symmetric cells and substantially improved capacity retention in both polyaniline/Zn and Na 0.33 V 2 O 5 /Zn full cells, whereas the faster (100) and (101) interfaces fail earlier. These findings establish a facet‐dependent kinetics–stability trade‐off and show that durable Zn anodes require coordinated control of charge transfer, dissolution topology, and crystallographic reconstruction.

title: Redirecting Excited‐State Energy Flow Through Programmed Supramolecular Confinement in Twisted Photosensitizers
abstract: ABSTRACT Programmed supramolecular confinement is introduced as a physical strategy to investigate aggregation‐enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)‐active twisted photosensitizers without changing the conjugated photosensitizing unit. In this design, TICT functions as a confinement‐sensitive regulator of excited‐state energy dissipation, while cell membranes (CM) serve as supramolecular platforms that confine photosensitizers within their compact phospholipid bilayer architectures. Through alkyl‐chain engineering, the obtained photosensitizers exhibit similar photophysical properties but tunable interactions with phospholipids, resulting in programmed confinement states within CMs. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that supramolecular confinement suppresses TICT‐mediated non‐radiative relaxation by reducing excitation‐induced donor‐acceptor torsional change and restricting intramolecular rotation, thereby redirecting excited‐state energy flow toward radiative emission and intersystem crossing‐mediated ROS generation. Accordingly, stronger confinement induces higher enhancements in fluorescence and ROS generation, establishing a supramolecular confinement‐dependent correlation among TICT restriction, fluorescence, and ROS generation. Finally, the optimized CM‐photosensitizer assemblies are applied as photodynamic systems and display effective performance in cancer immunotherapy. By coupling TICT restriction with ROS generation, this work establishes supramolecular confinement as a physical strategy for redirecting excited‐state energy flow and provides direct insight into how aggregation enhances ROS generation in twisted photosensitizers.

title: Metal‐Center‐Controlled Fenton‐Like Reactivity of Biomimetic First‐Row Transition Metal Complexes in Aqueous Anticancer Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS‐generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron‐mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water‐soluble biomimetic first‐row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine‐derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide‐activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N 2 Py 3 OH)] 2+ ( 1‐Fe ), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton‐like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi‐reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1‐Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1‐Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton‐like oxidative catalysis in redox‐based cancer therapy.

title: Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point‐of‐care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics‐based dual‐mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein‐containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false‐negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus ‐associated toxins and PMA‐treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein‐based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF‐based dual‐mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

title: Mechanophotochemistry : Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
abstract: ABSTRACT Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis , a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross‐coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution‐state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O 2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless‐steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light‐promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent‐minimized and viable alternative to solution‐state photochemical reactions.

title: Precision Matters: Minor Concentration Deviations of DMSO May Cause Major Efficacy Shifts
abstract: ABSTRACT Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) represents the most common solvent for dispersing hydrophobic materials in aqueous solutions for biological usage. Generally, a DMSO content of below 1% is believed to exert no effect on cells, and thus little attention is given to its influence on drug efficacy. title: Intrinsic Near‐Infrared Photothermal Effect Induces Single‐Crystal‐to‐Single‐Crystal Transformation in Organic Molecular Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR) light‐driven single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation holds profound significance for supramolecular chemistry and smart materials, yet remains a formidable challenge in purely organic molecular crystals. Herein, we demonstrate SCSC transformation driven by the intrinsic NIR photothermal effect of a rationally designed croconium derivative CR‐DPA‐OMe, which features strong NIR absorption and a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 60%. Solvated CR‐DPA‐OMe single crystals encapsulating CHCl 3 molecules exhibit exceptional ambient stability with crystallinity preserved for over two years. Benefiting from the robust dimeric packing of croconium motifs and the conformationally flexible methoxy‐substituted diphenylamine moieties, the resulting crystals successfully reconcile long‐range lattice order with structural flexibility, thus enabling efficient SCSC transformation upon NIR photothermal stimulation. Combined density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction analysis confirm that the transformation is driven by the synergistic interplay of photoinduced molecular conformational reorganization and photothermally‐converted heat, affording markedly faster transformation than conventional oven heating. Furthermore, tailored NIR irradiation enables spatiotemporally programmable guest release, demonstrating a remote manipulation inaccessible via macroscopic conductive heating. These findings highlight the substantial promise of NIR photothermal modulation as an emerging stimuli‐responsive strategy for precise structural engineering in molecular crystals, opening new avenues toward tailored functional material applications.

title: Ultra‐Low Thermal Conductivity in Mixed Anionic CuTe 2 Cl: Strong Antibonding States and Lone Pair‐Induced Te Ring Puckering
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal chalcohalides, an emerging class of mixed‐anion compounds, have recently garnered increasing interest as they unite the exceptional stability of metal chalcogenides with the versatile electronic tunability of metal halides. Here, we synthesize single‐ and polycrystalline CuTe 2 Cl, a two‐dimensional layered metal chalcohalide, which exhibits intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity ( κ lat ) of ∼0.54–0.24 W m −1 K −1 between 300 and 600 K along the layered growth direction. Strong p‐d* antibonding states arising from Cu 3 d ‐Te 5 p and Cu 3 d ‐Cl 3 p interactions in the valence band just below the Fermi level weaken the Cu‐Te and Cu‐Cl bonds to render the lattice elastically soft. Moreover, heteroleptic polyhedral coordination enforces chemical bonding hierarchy, which, together with the stereochemically active 5 s 2 lone pair of Te, generates pronounced lattice anharmonicity. These effects give rise to localized low‐energy optical phonon modes, which suppress the acoustic phonons, as confirmed by phonon dispersion calculations. 5 s 2 lone pair driven Te‐ring puckering and lattice shearing between layers provide low‐frequency optical modes, which are experimentally identified by low‐temperature Raman spectroscopy and heat‐capacity measurements. Collectively, strong p‐d* antibonding interaction induced lattice softening and lone pair driven instability produce strong anharmonicity, which markedly suppresses the heat‐carrying acoustic phonons, leading to intrinsically ultralow κ lat in mixed anionic CuTe 2 Cl.

title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

title: To reverse nature loss, change what drives it
abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability—it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.

title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe2/WS2 moiré superlattices
abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe 2 /WS 2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.
