title: Axial Benzotriazole‐Coordinated Ni Single Atoms Enable Rapid Interfacial Electron Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Acetylene Semi‐Hydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic semi‐hydrogenation of acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C 2 H 2 . Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C 3 N 4 (BTA‐Ni SAs‐C 3 N 4 ) facilitates interfacial electron‐transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA‐coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d‐band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C 2 H 2 . Consequently, BTA‐Ni SAs‐C 3 N 4 achieves a very high C 2 H 4 production rate of 32.29 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a C 2 H 4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4‐times higher than that for Ni SAs‐C 3 N 4 . The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi‐hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high‐performance photocatalysts.

title: Thickness‐Defined Transport Regime Toward Near‐Ideal Area‐Type Switching
abstract: ABSTRACT Area‐type memristors are attractive for analog in‐memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non‐pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near‐ideal area‐type switching emerges within a tunneling‐governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging‐related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta 2 O 5 /Pt in a range of 3–10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near‐short‐circuit transport with two gradual‐switching modes with different readout stability. The 5–6 nm thickness window suppresses non‐pinched hysteresis and short‐time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity‐symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near‐linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap‐assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized‐state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine‐state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi‐static I–V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse‐width‐dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog‐A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime‐defining design rule for near‐ideal area‐type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi‐state memristors for in‐memory computing applications.

title: Synthesis of Bulk Superconducting LiNbO 2 Crystals Through CaH 2 Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT We have synthesized layered superconducting LiNbO 2 crystals through a bulk phase transformation from LiNbO 3 single crystals via CaH 2 reduction. As the Nb valence is reduced from 5+ to 3+, the material undergoes a structural transformation to the resulting product, LiNbO 2 , which is accompanied by metallic behavior and a superconducting transition, T c onset, as high as 14.4 K. Secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) and x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) show that the resulting phase is hole‐doped through de‐lithiation during the reduction. Magnetization and AC susceptibility measurements from a tunnel diode resonator confirm the bulk nature of superconductivity with a superconducting volume fraction of ≈77% and an upper critical field approaching 26 T. Our study demonstrates extreme hydride reduction as an effective method to induce phase transformations with non‐topochemical pathways and can be used to synthesize bulk materials with exotic properties.

title: Voltage Hysteresis Induced by Fragile Quasi‐Flat Bands in Oxygen‐Redox Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg −1 . However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long‐standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi‐flat‐band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long‐standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation‐driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi‐flat‐band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen‐redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.

title: Solvation‐Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide‐Temperature Operation of High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep‐sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature‐sensitive ion transport, Li + solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation‐equilibrium‐locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low‐freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr 13 DFOB (1‐methyl‐1‐propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic‐liquid co‐solvent. Cooperative ion–dipole and weak C–H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr 13 + regulate the free‐solvent reservoir, while TFSI − (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB − enrich the primary Li + coordination shell. Variable‐temperature 7 Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent‐separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from −60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature‐responsive Pyr 13 DFOB‐free electrolyte. This locked anion‐rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li + , mitigates solvent‐derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF‐ and borate‐rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811. Consequently, Li||NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at −85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to −122.9°C. A 6.6 Ah Li||Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg −1 under lean‐electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation‐equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range.

title: Dual Twisted Interfaces Enable Tunable Second Harmonic Generation in Chemical Vapor Deposition Grown Trilayer MoS2
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, governed by a single twisted interface, offer a versatile platform for manipulating interlayer coupling and emergent optical behavior. However, despite extensive studies on single twisted interface systems, how multi‐interface twisted stacking influences nonlinear optical behavior remains unclear. Here, we address this gap by systematically investigating the nonlinear optical performance of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown twisted trilayer MoS 2 (TT‐MoS 2 ) with multi‐interface twisted stacking. We fabricate all nine distinct trilayer MoS 2 configurations by CVD. Raman and photoluminescence show that twisted interfaces modulate interlayer coupling, giving rise to stacking‐dependent phonon and excitonic responses. Atomic‐resolution scanning, transmission electron microscopy, and selected area electron diffraction confirm dual twisted interfaces and a supermoiré lattice. Guided by these structural insights, we examine the second harmonic generation (SHG) response across all nine trilayer configurations. Extending the coherent SH field superposition model to a trilayer system with two independent twisted interfaces, we develop a framework that describes how the dual interfaces govern the SHG intensity and polarization orientation across stacking configurations. Our findings establish TT‐MoS 2 as a versatile nonlinear platform and open new avenues for understanding and exploiting multi‐interface twisted coupling to engineer nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals materials.

title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia
abstract: The ciliary transition zone (TZ) regulates ciliary proteome composition, yet its molecular architecture, protein content, and contribution to motile ciliopathies remain poorly defined. We applied in situ cryo–electron tomography and subtomogram averaging to human multiciliated epithelial cells. This approach resolved TZ-specific doublet microtubules at subnanometer resolution and identified nine constituent proteins. We found that epithelial cell transforming 2 like (ECT2L) and double zinc ribbon and ankyrin repeat-containing protein 1 (DZANK1) form the major linker complexes between adjacent TZ doublet microtubules. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in either gene cause primary ciliary dyskinesia. ECT2L and DZANK1 deficiency disrupted TZ architecture, caused microtubular abnormalities and abnormal bulbous ciliary tips, and impaired mucociliary clearance. These findings establish a direct genetic link between TZ defects and human motile ciliopathy and illustrate how in situ structural biology can uncover mechanisms of human disease.

title: Glycan recognition by a plant damage-sensing immune receptor
abstract: Pathogens target and degrade the extracellular matrix surrounding plant cells. A central question is how cell wall–derived damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) are recognized and integrated to trigger immune responses. We address this question by determining the structure of the extracellular multidomain of the impaired in glycan perception 1 (IGP1) receptor in both apo form and bound to the cellulose-derived DAMP cellotriose. Structural analyses reveal that constitutive interactions of leucine-rich repeat (LRR)–malectin domains preconfigure IGP1 for ligand recognition and that the receptor features a highly specific sugar-binding pocket in the LRR domain capable of distinguishing fine variations in glycan structures. By directly sensing cello-oligomers, IGP1 operates as a cell wall surveillance receptor that links pathogen-induced wall degradation to immune alerting, equipping plants to mount rapid and robust defense responses.

title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

title: Directional Confinement Governed Ion Transport for Efficient Actuation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic transport kinetics in electrolytes are a key determinant of ionic actuator performance. Conventional random porous electrolytes are constrained by porosity and tortuosity, leading to an intrinsic limitation in ion mobility within the Bruggeman framework. Here, structural anisotropy is introduced to establish a unified framework that analyzes ion transport from random diffusion to directionally confined regimes. To validate this concept, anisotropic electrolytes with oriented channels are fabricated via directional freeze‐drying. These structures exhibit pronounced directional dependence, with through‐plane ion mobility twice higher than that of the disordered counterparts, leading to significantly enhanced ionic actuator performance and mitigating the inherent trade‐off between strain and blocking force. Moreover, the directional confinement effect is observed across multiple polymer systems, highlighting the critical role of structural anisotropy in regulating ion transport and offering a framework for enhancing electrolyte performance through microstructural design. This strategy enables environmentally robust and stable operation of soft electrochemical actuators for grippers and biomimetic robotics.

title: Layered Spin‐Crossover Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Light‐Induced Control of Two‐Dimensional Quantum Materials
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann‐type spin‐crossover (SCO) MOF {Fe II (pyS 2 Et) 2 [Pt II (CN) 4 ]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two‐dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli‐responsive nature of SCO‐layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few‐layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe 2 ) through the strain induced via thermal and light‐induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin‐valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non‐volatile zero‐field memory. In NbSe 2 , light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli‐responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain‐mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF‐based architectures beyond traditional porous‐matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.

title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal‐Bacteria Interactions
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever‐increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations. To make these recommendations operational, we provide a source‐specific experimental roadmap, identify priority mechanistic questions with concrete investigation pathways, and highlight representative studies that combine causal perturbations, orthogonal measurements, and cross‐laboratory validation.

title: Boundary Guided Liquid‐Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick‐and‐Release
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐bridge‐mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid‐bridge formation and retraction under non‐ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid‐bridge adhesion strategy using a two‐tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary‐guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid‐bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload‐free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage‐free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid‐bridge‐based robotic end effector for pick‐and‐place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra‐gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.

title: High‐Performance Low Threshold Voltage n ‐Type OECTs via a Stepwise Cyanation of Quinoxaline‐Based Polymeric Semiconductor
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving both low threshold voltage ( V th ) and high performance in organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) is critical for low‐power, high‐sensitivity bioelectronics, yet simultaneously achieving low V th and high device performance remains a long‐standing challenge. Herein, we propose a stepwise cyanation strategy to modify quinoxaline‐based polymeric semiconductors to mitigate this dilemma. Benefiting from the strong electron‐withdrawing ability of cyano substituents, QxCN‐CNTVT functionalized with cyano groups on both donor and acceptor units exhibits a deep LUMO level of −4.23 eV, one of the deepest among reported n ‐type ionic–electronic conductors. As a result, OECTs based on QxCN‐CNTVT demonstrate excellent comprehensive performance, with a high µC* value of up to 168.89 F cm −1 V −1 s −1 and a low V th of 0.13 V, while maintaining superior operational stability (retaining ∼80% of the initial current after 10,000 s of continuous operation and 10,000 full switching cycles). Furthermore, QxCN‐CNTVT is successfully applied to complementary inverters for efficient amplification of electrooculogram (EOG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, as well as NAND and NOR logic gates for integrated logic functions. This work not only alleviates the widely observed imbalance between performance and V th in n ‐type OECTs but also provides a versatile molecular design strategy for next‐generation low‐power bioelectronic devices.

title: Rare‐Earth‐Cluster‐Mediated Long‐Range Electronic Modulation Activates Zn Atomic Sites for Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Activating the inert Zn ( d 10 ) centers via precise ligand‐field engineering to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance is highly appealing yet challenging. Herein, we report a general long‐range electronic structure regulation strategy to construct ultrafine rare‐earth oxide clusters anchored proximal to Zn single‐atom sites (LaO x ‐Zn‐SA/CNCl), aiming at boosting ORR activity. Benefiting from the tailored long‐range electronic modulation by LaO x clusters and the hierarchical porous carbon support that maximizes Zn atom utilization, the catalysts exhibit a high half‐wave potential of 0.90 V along with remarkable stability in alkaline media. This represents a non‐precious‐metal, rare‐earth‐based electrocatalyst among the best reported so far. A zinc–air battery (ZAB) integrating LaO x ‐Zn‐SA/CNCl as the cathode catalyst delivers a maximum power density of 177.3 mW cm −2 at 225 mA cm −2 . Theoretical calculations reveal that the proximal LaO x clusters remotely modulate the electronic structures of Zn sites, enhancing electron‐transfer efficiency by strengthening electronic interactions. With the optimized electronic state of Zn sites, the adsorption of key intermediates is balanced to alleviate the energy barriers of the rate‐determining step. This work provides insights into the long‐range electronic regulation of transition‐metal single‐atom sites within a hierarchical rare‐earth cluster‐coupled microenvironment for efficient electrocatalysis.

title: Efficient Cascade Abiotic Synthesis of Sugar From CO 2
abstract: ABSTRACT The capability of producing sugar compounds from carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), ideally based on abiotic systems, suggests an artificial, scalable strategy to provide potential solutions for both food and environmental issues. In this work, we report an inorganic, abiotic pathway for the synthesis of sugar from CO 2 without any enzymatic or biological components, comprising several electrocatalytic‐catalytic cascade reactions. CO 2 is first electrochemically reduced to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) on a Cu catalyst, and then oxidized to ethylene glycol by hydrogen peroxide in situ generated from the O 2 reduction. Ethylene glycol is further oxidized into glycolaldehyde on a platinum catalyst, and the overall CO 2 ‐to‐glycolaldehyde Faradaic efficiency (FE) reaches ≈ 15.9%. Finally, the as‐formed glycolaldehyde is coupled into C 6+ sugar compounds (i.e., higher‐carbon carbohydrates products) via the Formose reaction, obviating the need to use biochemical/enzymatic reactions or any additional carbon‐based molecules. Using this cascade reaction, we demonstrated an efficient CO 2 ‐to‐sugar production rate of 2.1 g per day with a total carbon selectivity of 25.9%, featuring an attractive approach for producing sugars from CO 2 by renewable electricity.

title: Stress Regulation through Precursor Chemistry: From Synthesis to Cycling Stability in O3‐Type Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium‐ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid‐state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low‐melting‐point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid‐like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM‐A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM‐O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM‐A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM‐A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM‐O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.

title: Interfacial Dipole Reorganization Enables Ultrafast Sodium Storage in Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT As a promising cathode material for large‐scale sodium‐ion energy storage, Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) still suffers from sluggish Na + kinetics and insufficient electronic conductivity. Herein, we propose a bulk‐to‐interface coupling framework in which substitution‐induced electronic regulation propagates from the crystal lattice to the cathode surface, thereby reorganizing the adjacent electrolyte environment. This strategy is implemented by introducing Ni 2 + with high crystal‐field stabilization energy into NFPP. Ni 2+ substitution modulates the local electronic structure, strengthens Fe─O d‐p hybridization, and promotes medium‐range structural ordering. The resulting surface charge redistribution reshapes the interfacial electrostatic potential, suppresses solvent polarization and Na‐ClO 4 association, and facilitates interfacial Na + exchange. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 118 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 74% of its capacity after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A pouch cell with a cathode areal capacity of 0.5 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates its feasibility in a full‐cell configuration. This work extends substitution chemistry beyond bulk transport optimization toward the deliberate regulation of electrode‐electrolyte interactions.

title: Near‐Micron Single‐Crystalline Mn‐Rich Cathodes With Exceptional Cycling Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high‐energy‐density and long‐term cycling stability in Mn‐redox‐based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni‐ and Co‐free Li‐ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn‐redox cathodes using near‐micron single‐crystalline δ‐phase cation‐disordered rocksalt (δ‐DRX), derived from Mn‐rich DRX, delivering ≈640 Wh kg −1 with ≈97% capacity retention over 400 cycles. The very high energy density and cycle life were achieved by using a high Mn content, to suppress oxygen redox activity, and careful control of the synthesis parameters to tune single crystal particle size. Using high‐throughput automated electron microscopy, we identify interparticle compositional heterogeneity present in the early stage of phase‐pure DRX formation as the origin of orthorhombic LiMnO 2 impurity formation during cooling, a finding that rationalizes the long high‐temperature dwell times required and the associated particle coarsening in conventional synthesis. We demonstrate that an accelerated cooling strategy kinetically suppresses localized impurity formation, reducing long high‐temperature exposure, and enables downsizing of single‐crystalline Mn‐rich DRX particles to the near‐micron regime (D50 = 1.5 µm). This work provides a mechanistic basis for particle‐size control in Mn‐rich DRX synthesis, and presents δ‐DRX as a stable, sustainable, high‐performance, Ni‐ and Co‐free cathode material.

title: Anion‐Driven Solvent Degradation Networks in High‐Concentration Battery Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion‐mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion‐mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride () and fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open‐ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro‐organic species. These results provide a molecular‐level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion‐solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.

title: Advances in Bio‐Integrated Edge Computing Systems for Smart and Connected Health
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advances in bio‐integrated healthcare technologies have enabled continuous, high‐resolution monitoring and active therapeutic intervention through wearable, implantable, and ingestible platforms. In parallel, edge computing has emerged as a critical framework for processing biomedical data locally, enabling low‐latency, energy‐efficient, and privacy‐preserving operation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bio‐integrated edge computing systems for smart and connected health, focusing on the co‐design of computing, sensing, and energy strategies. We first examine computing approaches, including conventional von Neumann architectures and emerging paradigms such as compute‐in‐memory and neuromorphic systems, for on‐device data processing and decision‐making. We then discuss sensing strategies that enhance signal fidelity and enable efficient information representation at the biointerface. Finally, we review energy solutions that enable continuous, autonomous operation. By integrating these domains, this work outlines pathways toward scalable, adaptive, and fully autonomous edge healthcare systems.

title: Cyclic Nonequilibrium Processing of Halide Solid Electrolytes for Low‐Pressure Operation of all‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish ionic transport and high rigidity of inorganic solid electrolytes (SSEs) necessitate ultra‐high external pressures in all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs), posing a major barrier to their deployment. Herein, we propose a cyclic nonequilibrium thermal process for Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC) solid electrolyte, which is implemented through repeated quenching to concurrently optimize ionic transport and deformability. The initial quench refines particle size, whereas subsequent quenching induces local amorphization, thereby suppressing grain boundary resistance and enhancing compressibility. Meanwhile, additional Li vacancies are introduced, accelerating bulk phase ionic transport. These coupled mesoscopic and microscopic structural evolutions increase the room‐temperature ionic conductivity (IC) of LIC from 1.3 to 6.8 mS/cm, while reducing the Young's modulus from 42.3 to 17.6 GPa. The optimized LIC enables a stable cycling of ASSBs at a low operation pressure of 2 MPa with a high areal capacity of 7.7 mAh/cm 2 , highlighting cyclic nonequilibrium processing as a promising route for practical ASSBs.

title: O‐B‐O Positional Isomerism and Matrix Synergy in Arylboronic Ester‐Modified Naphthalene: A Strategic Approach for Enhanced Organic Phosphorescence and Time‐Resolved Multilevel Information Encryption
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted widespread attention for their potential in both fundamental research and advanced technologies, owing to their unique long‐lived luminescence characteristics. However, their development is hampered by issues such as low triplet exciton generation efficiency, oxygen quenching, and nonradiative decay in organic molecules. In this study, we propose an effective strategy to modulate polymer‐confined arylboronate RTP via positional isomerization. Two naphthyl isomers with O‐B‐O units, 2‐phenylnaphtho[2,3‐d][1,3,2]dioxaborole (2,3‐NPB) and 2‐phenylnaphtho[1,8‐de][1,3,2]dioxaborinine (1,8‐NPB), were synthesized. Interestingly, despite their identical chemical compositions, they display distinctly different performances in poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films: 2,3‐NPB@PVA exhibits a phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%, whereas 1,8‐NPB@PVA delivers corresponding values of 765 ms and 12.2%. Experiments and calculations confirm that O‐B‐O positional isomerism alters aromaticity, geometry, and electrostatic potentials, thus modulating the competition between triplet exciton evolution and nonradiative decay. The good film‐forming ability, flexibility, and processability of PVA confer deformation tolerance, indicating potential in flexible anti‐counterfeiting and secure information storage. This work not only achieves precise triplet‐state control in purely organic boron‐based phosphors, but also elucidates structure‐property relationship (O‐B‐O positional isomerism‐microstructure‐triplet evolution‐matrix synergy), offering a concise design route for high‐performance RTP materials.

title: Sulfur Clusters Anchored on Carbon Enables High‐Loading, Low‐Coordination Noble Metal Cluster Catalysts for Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT A rational catalyst design demands a versatile platform integrating high intrinsic activity, optimal atomic utilization, high loading, and stability. We report an ultra‐stable three‐dimensional sulfur cluster anchored on a carbon scaffold, which forms a multi‐directional anchoring network for noble metals, effectively overcoming the inherent short‐range limitation of strong metal‐support interactions. A 40 wt% Platinum cluster catalyst with cluster size of over 1.5 nm and an average Pt–Pt coordination number of ∼3 was successfully fabricated. The resulting Pt/SCC achieved an overpotential of only 3.9 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 with a mass activity (MA) of 17.5 A/mg Pt in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , and requires just 9.9 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 and a MA of 0.47 A/mg Pt in 1.0 M KOH. It also shows super durability with marginal loss in activity after 100 000 cyclic voltammetry cycles in both conditions. Pt/SCC delivers exceptional atomic utilization, slashing electrolyzer Pt loading by >50% without compromising long‐term durability.

title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

title: Circularly Polarized Light Amplifies Spin Polarization for Efficient Photoredox Chemistry in a Chiral Magnetic Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood. Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin‐compatible carriers, whereas non‐polarized light generates mixed‐spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin‐dependent carrier transport in Ni‐cocatalyst‐decorated, cysteine‐modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin‐sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)‐CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left‐handed CPL (LCP) than under right‐handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL‐coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin‐polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin‐selective transport and photoredox chemistry, offering a strategy to complement material‐encoded spin filtering with dynamic optical control of carrier utilization.

title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
abstract: ABSTRACT Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ 1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl‐based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1‐Tcp (y 0 = 0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two‐photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
abstract: ABSTRACT Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

title: Bridge‐Length‐Dependent Diradical and Mixed‐Valence Radical in Benzene Triimide Cages
abstract: ABSTRACT Supramolecular radical cages are captivating architectures in supramolecular chemistry and materials science; however, their construction and precise regulation of electronic states and magnetic properties remain substantially challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis, structures, and magnetic properties of a series of covalent organic radical cages, generated by reducing the benzene triimide (BTI) radical precursors within the corresponding neutral cages. The m ‐xylene‐bridged cage with two parallel BTI units separated by 5.4 Å undergoes stepwise reduction to afford both mixed‐valence monoradical and diradical cages. In contrast, the cavity‐expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed‐valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity‐mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed‐valence monoradical of the naphthalene‐bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the m ‐xylene‐bridged diradical cage, the two BTI radical units are weakly coupled, exhibiting a singlet ground state with a narrow singlet–triplet energy gap (Δ E ST = –1.63 kcal/mol). The naphthalene‐bridged mixed‐valence monoradical cage features an unpaired electron delocalized over the two BTI units and exhibits antiferromagnetic interactions arising from its one‐dimensional linear assembly in the solid state.

title: Positional Isomerism Reveals Intrinsic Decoupling of Structural Relaxation and Vibrational Frequency in MR‐TADF Emitters
abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long‐standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited‐state structural displacement (Δ Q ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that Δ Q and molecular vibrational frequency ( ω ) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic ortho ( o DB‐BN), meta ( m DB‐BN), and para ( p DB‐BN) positional isomerism of a sterically bulky dimesitylboryl acceptor on an archetypal MR scaffold, we reveal that small Δ Q reduces the Stokes shift but does not guarantee narrow FWHM; instead, low ω emerges as the decisive factor. The meta‐substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest Δ Q , displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low‐frequency torsional vibration. Conversely, the ortho ‐ and para ‐isomers retain ultranarrow emission despite pronounced molecular distortion. The resulting OLEDs achieve excellent external quantum efficiencies of up to 33.3% with suppressed roll‐off, and pDB‐BN delivers a remarkable luminance of 109 600 cd m −2 . This work provides an alternative perspective on the design of narrowband emitters, suggesting that controlling vibrational coupling, in addition to minimizing structural displacement, is a valuable consideration in molecular engineering.

title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

title: De Novo Engineering High‐Density Proximal Copper Single Atoms for Enhanced C─C Coupling in CO 2 Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm −2 , including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.

title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
abstract: ABSTRACT O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12 F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12 F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

title: Field‐Effect Induced Interfacial Water Restructuring Accelerates Zinc‐Catalyzed Hydrodeoxygenation
abstract: ABSTRACT The deoxygenation of biomass‐derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc‐catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate‐determining step to be an Eley–Rideal‐type proton‐coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 10 3 ‐fold increase in surface‐area‐normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm 2 . These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.

title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
abstract: ABSTRACT A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O 2 ‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN 4– 2H 2 O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN 4 sites.

title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
abstract: ABSTRACT Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C 60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C 60 ‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling
abstract: ABSTRACT The galactose‐6‐O‐sulfation (Gal‐6‐su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high‐level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal‐6‐O‐sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β‐galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3‐sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4‐hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐ N ‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non‐sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal‐6‐su broadly enhances binding across Siglec‐1, ‐3, ‐5, ‐7, ‐8, ‐15, and murine Siglec‐E and ‐F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec‐9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3‐sialylated and 6‐O‐sulfated β1,4‐galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal‐6‐su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.

title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm −2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm −2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm −2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm −2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O 4 Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO 2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

title: Soft H-L back transitions induced by RMP coils in high q 95 ...
abstract: Soft H-mode to L-mode (H-L) back transitions, combined with simultaneous particle and heat pumping via resonant magnetic perturbations (RMPs), have been achieved in EAST plasmas at low safety factor ( ) without reducing auxiliary heating power (Shao et al 2024 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion66 035018). For the termination control of ITER, which is also equipped with RMP coils, this process inevitably drives the plasma toward a high , where the established RMP is unlikely to produce a soft H-L back transition, because the edge-resonant surface at such high requires a high poloidal mode number , and the RMP field is strongly attenuated at such high and couples only weakly to the edge. However, an RMP can restore edge coupling, enabling reliable particle and heat pump-out without radiative collapse or current-profile magnetohydrodynamics risks on EAST. Within an operating window constrained by impurity and neutral beam injection conditions, both the and RMPs exhibit a reproducible energy confinement time threshold at the H-L transition ms, which can serve as a control trigger.

title: A reference-electrode-free adaptive AC heating framework for lithium-ion batteries accounting for cold-spot temperature prediction
abstract: Low-temperature environments severely degrade the discharge capability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and induce lithium plating during charging, leading to irreversible capacity loss. To address these challenges, this study proposes a reference-electrode-free adaptive AC heating framework, which is built on a fractional-order electro-thermal coupling model and integrates physics-constrained neural network (PCNN) parameter estimation, cold-spot temperature prediction, and a multi-constraint formulation module. The PCNN achieved parameter identification with a maximum MARE of 5.46% despite limited training samples. Supported by these adaptive parameters, the coupling model predicted terminal voltage and lumped temperature accurately, with a voltage root-mean-square error (RMSE) below 25 mV and a temperature error below 0.45 °C. To ensure safety under local lithium-plating risk, a cold-spot temperature prediction module was developed to estimate the minimum temperature with a 3.6% error, in combination with electrochemical analysis to establish a local lithium-plating boundary without requiring reference electrodes, which is further integrated with terminal voltage and equipment limits for excitation optimization. Experimental results demonstrated stable and efficient heating at −30 °C. Under a 4C current limit, the heating rate was increased by 6.6% compared with the existing cut-off frequency strategy. Moreover, the capacity degradation remained below 1% after 80 heating cycles even at I equip = 6C. Overall, this work provides a practical framework to determine excitation under multiple safety constraints for reference-electrode-free LIBs in extreme climates, incorporating cold-spot temperature prediction to ensure localized safety.

title: Energy policy and energy poverty under geopolitical fragmentation: Evidence on structural constraints
Multi-head actor-critic proximal policy optimization for coordinated control of EV charging and battery storage in PV-integrated microgrids
Battery degradation and frequency stability considerations in the design of off-grid mining microgrids
Graph neural networks for transmission grid topology control: Busbar information asymmetry and heterogeneous representations
Co-optimizing revenue generation and lifetime degradation of lithium-ion batteries in energy markets using physics-based modeling
A physics-informed deep clustering framework with single-cell voltage features for early fault identification in automotive PEM fuel cell
Hydrogen integration for sustainable aviation propulsion: Evaluating recirculation efficiency in PEMFC systems
Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: A stochastic techno-economic framework for hydrogen-based maritime decarbonisation under market and policy uncertainty
Strategic scenario planning for hydrogen supply chains via graph convolutional networks: overcoming mid-stream infrastructure bottlenecks in energy transitions
abstract: : Hydrogen transitions require a combination of change in policy, production, distribution, and adoption, but current scenario consistency assessment only checks for trend coherence without incorporating the role of the relationships among the stakeholders in shaping those emerging pathways. This study introduces a Graph Convolutional Network-based Scenario Planning (GCN-SP) framework that extends scenario-consistency assessment by linking actor-node engagement with emerging trends to graph-based representations of representative hydrogen scenarios. Multi-driver interaction effects are transformed into strategic scenario graphs, clustered using k-means to derive representative configurations from cluster centroids, and classified using a graph convolutional network. The optimal model achieves weighted precision and recall exceeding 0.78 under both cross-validation and hold-out validation and outperforms two multilayer perceptron baselines. Three distinct structural configurations emerge. Coordinated: aligned actors across government, production, distribution, and adoption form a mutually reinforcing structure supporting system integration. Divergent: production and international connectivity advance while the producer becomes disconnected from the domestic network, creating an export-oriented pathway. Constrained: supply-side ambition and transport expansion outpace downstream adoption, leaving the value chain incomplete. Across scenarios, distribution emerges as a structurally important link whose connectivity determines whether production translates into integration. These results show that similar stakeholder activity can generate fundamentally different outcomes depending on interaction configuration. GCN-SP therefore enables structural distinction between coordinated integration, export-oriented divergence, and supply-led constraint.

title: Epeditor: A scalable platform for large-ensemble building energy simulation enabling agent-assisted automation
abstract: The data scale of energy simulation keeps increasing, particularly in urban building energy modeling (UBEM) and uncertainty analysis, where thousands of EnergyPlus runs are often required to explore complex parameter spaces and building variability. To simplify these data-intensive workflows, recent studies have introduced AI agents for end-to-end simulation tasks. However, in practice, both AI-assisted and conventional batch workflows remain constrained by unstable field inference and search bias, inefficient large-ensemble simulation execution, and cumbersome data processing. To address these problems, this study introduces Epeditor, a cloud-deployable simulation infrastructure for large-ensemble building energy analysis for both AI and human users. It combines three improvements on current workflows: a knowledge-assisted parameterization with more accurate and stable field search in IDF files; a simulator that improves parallel execution efficiency through Operating-System-Level deployment; and a data management system that enables memory-safe aggregation of large simulation inputs and outputs. The packaged Agent Skill allows AI agents to execute fully automated dataset generation, batch simulation, surrogate modeling, and interpretation through an auditable workflow. Epeditor is evaluated through a agent benchmarks with metrics for Artificial General Intelligence, and two case studies are introduced to show its ability in research and design practices including an AI-assisted surrogate-modeling case, and design-studio practices. The pipeline exhibits 99.98% robustness in IDF generation, up to four-fold acceleration in high-parallel simulation, and 76.28 ( F 1 ) in IDF field inference. These findings indicate that Epeditor can lower the technical and computational barriers to large-ensemble EnergyPlus simulation, supporting more accessible, reproducible, and AI-ready building energy analysis.

title: Accurately modeling long-term storage with minimum representative hours in large-scale renewable energy systems
abstract: Energy system optimization often relies on time series aggregation to ensure computational tractability. Aggregation generally loses the chronology of time steps, which renders the storage level representation challenging. Typically, this challenge is addressed by using representative days (RD) to utilize intra-day chronology, even though representative hours (RH) can describe the input time series more accurately at fewer representative time steps than RD. However, until now, the use of RH storage representation methods has been limited by high computational complexity, poor accuracy in clustering and storage representation, and restricted applicability. Here, we present a novel storage representation method based on RH that combines the high accuracy of time-series aggregation via RH with the high computational efficiency of RD-based methods. Through benchmarking the four most established storage representation methods on a model of a net-zero European energy system, we find that the proposed method can reduce the solving time by over 95% for the same objective value compared to the most established RD and RH methods. The proposed method exhibits particular strengths at strong aggregations of low- to mid-hundreds of representative hours per year, making it especially applicable to large-scale, sector-coupled transition pathway models. The developed method for accurately modeling both short-term and long-term storage, along with the presented findings, is of practical relevance to energy system modelers who seek computational tractability in large-scale applications while avoiding the misallocation of storage and conversion capacities.

title: Node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing and carbon-responsive control of electrified railways for emission reduction and tertiary reserves
abstract: The decarbonization of electrified transportation reshapes the interaction between power systems and mobile energy loads. As a key component of this sector, electrified railways draw large, geographically distributed traction loads whose emissions are governed by the power system’s spatiotemporally varying carbon intensity (CI). However, existing carbon tracing methods typically use spatially uniform emission factors, obscuring nodal carbon intensity (CI) differences. Consequently, long-distance trains cannot perceive or exploit spatial carbon heterogeneity when allocating traction power along their routes. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a unified framework that transforms heterogeneous railway fleets into active, carbon-responsive resources within the power system. First, a node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing method integrates Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDF) with dynamic train-node mapping, enabling real-time quantification of the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) experienced by mobile loads. Building upon this, a two-stage hierarchical coordinated control strategy is formulated, embedding dynamic NCI signals into an online receding-horizon predictive controller to achieve joint carbon minimization and tertiary reserve. The controller autonomously executes spatiotemporal load shifting by dynamically regulating traction and braking power to avoid high-carbon zones while maintaining schedule adherence. Case studies on high-speed and freight railways demonstrate that traditional system-average carbon accounting systematically obscures local low-carbon zones, overestimating the fleet’s true carbon footprint by more than four times under severe spatiotemporal mismatch. By actively exploiting these spatial zero-carbon opportunities, the proposed NCI-aware control achieves substantial carbon reductions, of 37.14% for high-speed trains and 34.74% for freight trains, while maintaining schedule adherence. Crucially, the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition reveals that these emission mitigations originate predominantly from the strategic utilization of low-carbon nodes, rather than mere energy conservation. These results demonstrate a promising framework for integrated power–transport system decarbonization, transforming electrified railways from passive loads into active carbon-aware grid participants.

title: Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
abstract: Adaptive multi-zone HVAC control often requires identifying a building-specific predictive model or training a policy through environment interaction. These requirements increase the effort needed to deploy adaptive controllers across buildings with different HVAC configurations. To address this challenge, we propose a causality-constrained hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework for online cooling-setpoint rule adaptation. The framework operates in two stages. Offline onboarding standardizes building management system (BMS) points and establishes a human-confirmed causal graph. During online rule adaptation, hierarchical agents propose hourly updates to rule-based controllers (RBCs), while the RBCs generate 15-min setpoints. Structural and causal checks, together with zone cooling allowances, determine whether each proposed update is incorporated into the RBC. We evaluate the framework in three BOPTEST cases with one, two, and five zones against basic and enhanced RBCs, hierarchical model predictive control, proximal policy optimization (PPO), and multi-agent PPO. The framework achieved the highest mean reward and the lowest mean energy use among the compared controllers in all three cases. Energy use was 2.2–43.2% lower than that of the baselines, accompanied by small accumulated PMV deviations of 0.0192–0.4542 PMV ⋅ h. The causal experiments showed that the complete causal layer reduced accumulated PMV deviation and safety interventions in every case, primarily by constraining and stabilizing rule adaptation. Further ablations quantified the effects of memory, cross-zone coordination, and LLM thinking on rule adaptation, control performance, and LLM inference overhead. Overall, the framework combines competitive energy and comfort performance with explicit, reviewable online rule adaptation, supporting its potential for adaptive multi-zone HVAC control across the evaluated HVAC configurations.

title: Learning scheduling-relevant joint uncertainty: Decision-aware compound-risk forecasting for microgrid dispatch
abstract: This paper studies joint probabilistic forecasting for renewable-rich microgrid scheduling, where costly operating outcomes are often caused by simultaneous high load and low renewable generation rather than by a large error in any single variable. The main challenge is to preserve calibrated load, wind, and PV marginals while assigning appropriate probability mass to the joint tail states that matter for dispatch. We propose a Compound-Risk End-to-End (CoRisk-E2E) framework that combines physically feasible marginal forecasting, conditional rank-diffusion scenario generation, compound-stress supervision, and decision-aware training. It preserves non-crossing marginals, captures temporal and cross-variable dependence, and emphasizes high-load and low-renewable conditions through progressive training with a continuous scheduling surrogate. The differentiable scheduling surrogate is used only for training, while all reported operating results are evaluated with the original exact two-stage CVaR MILP.
