abstract: Publication date: Available online 16 October 2026Source: Physics Letters BAuthor(s): M. Zeeshan Gul, Sadia Zahid, Faisal Javed, Azzh Saad Alshehry, Noura M. Alhouiti, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov

title: A Fluorine-Free Electrolyte with Copper Ion-Guided Interfacial Regulation Enables Ultra-Stable Zinc Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Non-aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a promising pathway toward high energy density and long-lasting energy storage systems, yet their practical implementation is hindered by dendritic growth and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Herein, we report a fluorine-free organic electrolyte based on zinc methanesulfonate (ZMS), (Zn(MeSO3)2, in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), coupled with a copper ion (Cu2+) additive to regulate the zinc (Zn) deposition via interfacial engineering. The ZMS salt provides a tunable electrolyte environment, while the Cu2+ additive undergoes a spontaneous galvanic replacement reaction with Zn, forming a Cu-based interfacial layer. This interfacial modification promotes uniform Zn nucleation and suppresses dendritic growth. The optimized 5 mM CuSO4 electrolyte delivers 99.88% CE and enables ultra-stable Zn||Zn cycling (>2000 h), while sustaining operation up to 20 mA cm–2. The complementary spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses support the formation of a Cu-based interfacial layer and reveal modified methanesulfonate transport in the Cu2+-containing electrolyte. The full cells with both NaV3O8 and PANI cathodes achieve 74.2% capacity retention (relative to first-cycle capacity) over 300 cycles and 92.6% retention over 800 cycles, respectively, demonstrating proof-of-concept full-cell compatibility of this fluorine-free electrolyte formulation with different cathode chemistries.

title: High-Performance Self-Powered PbSe/Ag2Se Heterojunction Photodetector Enabled by Annealing-Induced in Situ Electrode Phase Conversion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lead selenide (PbSe) thin films are attractive for room-temperature infrared photodetection, yet efficient self-powered operation relies on the construction of a high-quality heterojunction. Herein, an asymmetric Ag/PbSe/Ni electrode structure was fabricated and subsequently annealed in an O2 atmosphere, inducing Ag diffusion into the PbSe film and in situ phase conversion at the Ag/PbSe interface to form Ag2Se. As a result, a high-quality Ag/Ag2Se/PbSe/Ni heterojunction was directly constructed. Under zero bias and 1550 nm illumination, the device exhibits an ultralow dark current of 1.61 × 10–9 A, an Ion/Ioff ratio of 521, detectivity of 7.73 × 1010 Jones, and responsivity of 8.78 mA/W, demonstrating excellent self-powered infrared photodetection performance. Notably, the Ag electrode serves not only as an electrical contact but also as a precursor for heterojunction formation through in situ phase conversion, simplifying device fabrication while simultaneously improving photoresponse performance. First-principles calculations further corroborate that the robust built-in electric field at the heterojunction interface facilitates carrier separation. This work provides a simple and cost-effective strategy for developing high-performance, low-power-consumption self-powered infrared photodetectors.

title: Enhanced Dielectric and Thermal Properties of PVDF-AlN Films for Flexible Dual-Mode Sensors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF), known for flexible wearable sensors and capacitive pressure sensing applications, stands out due to its premier piezoelectric property and excellent biocompatibility. However, the widespread deployment of PVDF-based devices is severely hindered by its inherent low dielectric constant, high dielectric loss, and poor thermal conductivity, which limit sensor sensitivity and response speed. In this paper, we propose a strategy to fabricate large-area high-performance AlN nanoflower-doped PVDF (APVDF) composite films, obtained with excellent dielectric properties (22 and 0.17 @ 1 Hz) and a low driving electric field of 40 MV/m. Especially, the bulk thermal conductivity reaches 14.97 W/(m·K), which is nearly 7% higher than that of commercial PVDF. Herein, the unique hierarchical nanoflower structure formed by selective oxidation of AlN may not only enhance the electroactive β + γ phase of PVDF but also constructs continuous thermal-conductive pathways to improve its heat-dissipation capability. Next, the APVDF-based dual-mode (pressure and electric field) sensor exhibits a fast piezoelectric response (20 ms) and high electric-field sensitivity (3.45 × 10−3 pF/(V/mm)) in a low-frequency range (1−10 Hz). This work paves the way for next-generation wearable electronics, human−machine interfaces, and tactile sensing systems, offering a solution to address the long-standing limitations of PVDF in advanced functional applications.

title: Flexible 2D Perovskite–hBN Optoelectronic Dendritic Neurons for Energy-Efficient Information Processing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial dendrites, capable of nonlinear signal integration, are key building blocks for next-generation neuromorphic hardware, yet their realization in soft, solution-processed materials remains hindered by instability and poorly controlled ion dynamics. Here, we report an artificial dendrite element based on a vertically orchestrated ITO/Ag nanoparticle (NP)/hBN/(PEA)2MA4Pb5I16/Pt NPS/ITO heterostructure, where a monolayer hBN barrier governs metal-ion injection with atomic precision. The hBN-mediated field redistribution enables graded and time-dependent filament initiation within the oriented two-dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite, producing highly nonlinear current integration analogous to excitatory postsynaptic potentials. Under consecutively correlated stimuli, the device exhibits hallmark dendritic behaviors—temporal summation, threshold-dependent firing, refractory period, and wavelength-sensitive integration—arising from controlled Ag+ accumulation and reversible filament branching. The devices operate at ∼1 V, demonstrate stable and reproducible transient responses over >1011 cycles, and retain robust performance under mechanical deformation. Complementary physics-based numerical modeling and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the influence of hBN on Ag+ diffusivity, as well as on filament formation. The dendritic neurons can efficiently encode velocity and direction, enabling compact feature maps for accurate motion classification and trajectory tracking. Our results introduce a promising material platform for high-density, energy-efficient neuromorphic processors capable of bio-inspired spatiotemporal learning.

title: Deep Learning-Assisted Noise-Robust Optical Encryption Enabled by Pentachromatic Phototransistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Optical communication requires effective encryption strategies for secure information transmission. The use of different wavelengths allows optical information to be configured in different ways, while broadband photoresponse enables these wavelength signals to be detected within a single device. Based on this approach, this study fabricated a broadband transparent phototransistor that operates across ultraviolet to infrared wavelengths. The IGZO/Ag2O/IGZO stacked structure exhibited a lower oxygen-related defect component and improved device stability. The responsivity increased by a factor of 2.38 and the noise equivalent power decreased by a factor of 1.95 compared to the IGZO/Ag2O device. The broadband photoresponse properties of the device enabled the separation of key and data channels, while a dynamic key enhanced security. This approach restricts pattern recognition compared to using fixed keys, resulting in a higher security rate. The learning-based approach was evaluated under noise and sensitivity-drift conditions, together with the effect of photoresponse stability under repetitive operation. These results contribute to the fabrication of broadband transparent phototransistors, facilitating high-performance optical encryption systems.

title: Nanoparticle Surface Curvature Impacts the Synthesis of Polymer Brushes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface-initiated ring-opening metathesis polymerization (SI-ROMP) is a powerful method for grafting polymers with different macromolecular architectures and chemical compositions onto surfaces, offering the potential to design hybrid materials with tailored properties. However, inherent challenges remain, especially regarding secondary metathesis reactions, resulting in lower graft polymer conversion, broader molecular weight distributions, and the formation of free polymer. Here, we report that surface curvature plays a critical role in the graft-from polymerization of poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD)-grafted silica nanoparticles, where nanoparticles with high curvature (i.e., smaller diameters) reach targeted molecular weights and graft densities, and calculated dry brush heights, which is ascribed to fewer interchain cross-metathesis occurrences. SI-ROMP was conducted on a series of silica particles with diameters ranging from 13 to 128 nm, representing surfaces that are highly curved to essentially flat, respectively. The nanoparticle curvature was quantified by the ratio of the nanoparticle radius (R) to the dry brush height (h), where R/h values much greater than 1 signify a “flat” surface. Smaller particles (e.g., 13 nm diameter), with higher surface curvature (R/h ≈ 1), demonstrated more successful grafting and higher polymer conversion compared to larger particles with flatter surfaces (R/h ≈ 10). ReaxFF-based reactive molecular dynamics simulations revealed that polymer chain grafting density, which controls neighboring chain proximity, directly affects the propensity of secondary metathesis. Fewer secondary metathesis events occur as the spacing between neighboring polymer chains increases. The findings highlight the role of propagating chain proximity in facilitating or deterring secondary metathesis, which influences the uniformity of graft chains and polymerization efficiency. The effects of particle surface curvature in surface-initiated polymerizations, particularly with respect to SI-ROMP, are an overlooked parameter, yet provide a path forward for improving graft quality on lower curvature surfaces.

title: Nanocellulose-Integrated BioClay to Improve Stability and Efficacy in RNA Interference-Mediated Antiviral Protection of Plants
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract RNA interference (RNAi) technology offers a nontransgenic and sequence-specific strategy for plant protection, but its foliar application in the field is limited by rapid RNA degradation and poor persistence on leaf surfaces. Here, we developed a nanocellulose-enabled clay-based platform for double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) foliar delivery, named as BioClay@CNF, that offers dsRNA persistence on leaves and durable antiviral activity in plants. Incorporation of nanocellulose fibers (CNFs) increased dsRNA retention and resisted rain-induced wash-off while simultaneously shielding dsRNA from enzymatic and thermal degradation under fluctuating pH and humidity conditions. The fibrous CNF network enhanced water retention and rehydration of the formulation on the leaf surface, which may help maintain local dsRNA availability under fluctuating environmental conditions. Using the cucumber mosaic virus as a model system, BioClay@CNF exhibited 85.1% viral inhibition for 20 days while significantly reducing visual damage and increasing leaf dry weight with higher chlorophyll content. These findings demonstrated that BioClay@CNF offers a promising strategy for sustainable management of plant virus diseases.

title: High-Throughput Screening of a Lipid Nanoparticle (LNP) Library Identifies Lead Formulations for CRISPR-Cas9 Ribonucleoprotein Delivery and Gene Editing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) using synthetic materials can bypass the host translational machinery and limit the duration of genomic exposure, minimizing the risk of off-target mutations. Despite their advantages, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery that achieve highly efficient editing at low doses remain limited. In the present study, we developed a library of ionizable lipids (ILs) and corresponding LNPs to enhance the delivery and editing efficiencies of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complexes. Following comprehensive in vitro screening and formulation optimization, an optimal LNP candidate containing the C12A9 IL (denoted as LNPC12A9) was identified that achieved ∼90% EGFP disruption in HEK293T-EGFP cells at an RNP concentration of 30 nM and ∼60% at 15 nM. The editing performance was consistently observed at an RNP concentration of 15 nM when editing the Gcgr and HPRT1 genes across multiple hepatic cell lines. Moreover, coencapsulation of RNP and a single-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (ssODN) template for homology-directed repair (HDR) within LNPC12A9 induced an HDR rate of 37.8%. Systemic administration of LNPC12A9 into C57BL/6J mice led to liver tropism and a total hepatic Pcsk9 gene disruption rate of 1.39%. In conclusion, this study provides insights into the construction of an LNP platform to improve the delivery efficiency of CRISPR-Cas9 RNP, thereby facilitating the development of LNPs for safe, precise, and tissue-specific Cas9 RNP-based genome editing therapies.

title: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Stem cell–based therapies offer potential for repairing large skeletal defects, yet persistent inflammation limits their efficacy. Here, we identify macrophage–derived IL-18 as an immune switch that impairs skeletal regeneration by disrupting immune–mesenchymal cell interactions. IL-18 is elevated in male mouse non-healing models and human bone nonunion samples, supporting its translational relevance. Mechanistically, IL-18 acts as an upstream amplifier of inflammation by inducing Serpina3f transcription, thereby driving macrophage senescence and M1 polarization and triggering a feed-forward inflammatory cascade that suppresses mesenchymal stem/stromal cell osteogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays further show that IL-18 directly impairs mesenchymal stem/stromal cell proliferation, clonogenicity, and mitochondrial fitness. Genetic deletion of IL-18 restores regenerative potential, whereas pharmacological blockade with IL-18–neutralizing antibodies or IL-18 binding protein reverses macrophage dysfunction and promotes bone healing. These findings establish IL-18 as a key mediator of inflammation–induced regenerative failure and a potential therapeutic target for skeletal regeneration.

title: Target trial emulation of effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy in four European countries
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Evidence on real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy remains limited. Using health data from the UK, Sweden, Spain, and Norway, we emulated two target trials to estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines administered during pregnancy against COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation, and admission to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The first trial compares initiation of a primary (two-dose) vaccination with unvaccinated, and the second compares the receipt of a first booster (third dose) with unboosted after primary vaccination. Pregnant women receiving a first or booster vaccination were matched weekly to comparable unexposed pregnant women. A total of 62,061 and 41,096 pregnant women were included in the first and second trial, respectively. Meta-analysis across the four databases showed a VE for primary vaccination of 26·2% (95% CI 16·2–35·1) against infection and 55·6% (95% CI 44·1–64·8) against hospitalisation. For boosters, the VE was 33.6% (95% CI 1·6–56·6) against infection and 34·1% (95% CI 0·6–56·4) against hospitalisation. ICU admission outcomes were too rare to analyse. In this work, we show that primary and first-booster mRNA vaccination during pregnancy is associated to a lower risk of COVID-19-related hospitalisation, while protection against infection is more modest and heterogeneous across databases.

title: Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group (p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

title: Cell-free reconstitution reveals synergistic stabilization of microtubule doublets by PACRG and FAP20
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

title: Precision RNAi for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in mice using a combinatorial unimolecular allele selective approach
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva is a rare genetic disorder caused primarily by the ACVR1R206H mutation, resulting in debilitating heterotopic ossification triggered by inflammatory flare-ups. Here, we report a disease-modifying, allele-selective small interfering RNA targeting ACVR1R206H while preserving wildtype ACVR1 function. Docosanoic acid-conjugated ACVR1 small interfering RNA, alone or combined with one targeting the pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-1β, reduced heterotopic ossification in a murine model using both post-trauma and preventative strategies. Combination therapy was more effective than either pathway alone. We further developed lipophilic divalent molecules targeting both pathways in a single compound. These showed comparable muscle accumulation and efficacy to the combined monovalent forms following local and systemic administration, while enabling equimolar dosing and simplified manufacturing. Treatment suppressed inflammatory, WNT, Notch, Hedgehog, and transforming growth factor β signaling in fibroadipogenic progenitors, reducing cartilage, bone, and connective tissue formation. This work establishes a platform for disease-modifying therapies in this and other musculoskeletal disorders.

title: One Health in action: regional innovations and shared challenges in addressing antimicrobial resistance
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries, yet perspectives and innovations from these regions remain underrepresented. During World Antimicrobial Awareness Week 2025, the AMR Knowledge Hub convened a four-day webinar series on AMR challenges and One Health solutions across three regions, with a country spotlight on Nigeria. Discussions highlight critical gaps in political commitment, sustainable financing, and locally relevant evidence, particularly on antibiotic stewardship. Regional and country experiences demonstrate the importance of context-specific research, locally driven innovation, and stronger governance. Integrating these voices into global AMR governance is essential for a more equitable, effective, and enduring response.

title: Sequential Dual Nanoparticle Approach for Extracellular Matrix Remodeling and Targeted Chemotherapy through Liposome–Exosome Hybridization in Pancreatic Cancer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant malignancies, with a poor prognosis and limited response to conventional therapies. Although liposomal doxorubicin (DOX) formulations reduce systemic toxicity, their clinical use is constrained by insufficient tumor targeting and poor intratumoral penetration. Here, we report a sequential dual-nanoparticle approach that integrates extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling with tumor-targeted chemotherapy to overcome these barriers. Hyaluronidase-loaded liposomes (LH) were first employed to degrade hyaluronic acid–rich ECM, followed by the administration of DOX-loaded liposome–exosome hybrid nanoparticles (HLD) engineered using pancreatic cancer cell–derived exosomes to confer intrinsic tumor-homing capability. The DOX-loaded hybrid nanoparticles demonstrated enhanced cellular uptake, potent cytotoxicity, and strong immunogenic cell death (ICD) responses in pancreatic cancer cells. ECM degradation by LH significantly improved intratumoral accumulation and penetration of subsequently administered HLD in vivo. In a pancreatic cancer xenograft model, sequential LH and HLD treatment resulted in superior tumor growth suppression compared with monotherapies, without inducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work demonstrates a modular, sequential nanotherapeutic platform that synergistically combines ECM remodeling and exosome-mediated targeting, offering a promising strategy to improve drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy in stromal-dense solid tumors, such as pancreatic cancer.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Bacterial Surfaces and Barriers: Biogenesis and Pathogen–Host Interactions
abstract: Abstract The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.

title: Robust van der Waals diamond-like dielectric for two-dimensional electronics
abstract: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. Here, we report fluorinated diamane, a diamond-like van der Waals material, as a high-performance gate dielectric. By combining a high dielectric constant, exceptional breakdown strength, and efficient heat dissipation, fluorinated diamane integrates seamlessly with diverse two-dimensional semiconductors and memory devices. This material platform addresses long-standing dielectric bottlenecks in ultra-scaled two-dimensional electronics.

title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

title: PhD students who write dissertation with AI less likely to stay in academia
abstract: US PhD graduates who used artificial intelligence were more likely to work in industry.

title: Unprecedented atlas explores mitochondria across the tree of life
abstract: The mitoproteomes of five parasites and a plant hold medical potential — and reignite the question of just when the mitochondrion evolved.

title: Rewilding the atoll engine
abstract: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience.

title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
abstract:
Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ
                    L
                    , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing–based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ
                    L
                    to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ
                    L
                    to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ
                    L
                    to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active
abstract: Data from mouse brains and 13 human brains show a link between levels of a lipid-degrading enzyme and cognitive resilience.

title: IceCube just won a Nobel prize. Protect astroparticle physics projects with the same potential
abstract: Building the Nobel-prizewinning neutrino experiment was a big risk. To continue its success, scientists — and funders — need to stay bold.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: SPRIZ (CCDC127) protein conserved in deuterostome animals is a rigid OMM–IMM tether that locally sets mitochondrial IMS volume
abstract:
The double-membrane nature of mitochondria generates an intermembrane volume through which ions, reactive oxygen species, and metabolites must flux to reach the matrix or cytosol, but whether this volume is a genetically specified structure remains unknown. We identify SPRIZ (spatial regulator of the intermembrane zone), the product of
                    Ccdc127
                    , a gene conserved across deuterostome animals. SPRIZ assembles into an ∼18-nanometer homodimeric tether anchored in the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) and inserted into the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) through vertebrate-specific hydrophobic loops, physically spacing the two membranes and setting local intermembrane volume. Cryo-electron tomography of native mitochondria revealed rod-like densities spanning the intermembrane space (IMS), consistent with SPRIZ’s predicted rigid coiled-coil architecture and membrane-spanning topology. In mouse liver, two-dimensional morphometry measured ∼3-fold expansion of IMS area with SPRIZ and ∼5.5-fold with lengthened mitochondrial artificial increaser of the IMS (MARTINI); 3D electron tomography confirmed MARTINI’s greater OMM–IMM separation and normalized IMS volume. This expansion was functionally validated by increased
                    14
                    C-mannitol accessibility to the IMS and by impaired mitochondrial Ca
                    2+
                    uptake. Constitutive
                    Ccdc127/SPRIZ
                    knockout produced viable mice and, in liver mitochondria, preserved overall ultrastructure but caused modest IMS expansion, consistent with loss of local OMM–IMM constraints that stabilize membrane geometry at discrete sites. We therefore identify IMS volume as a genetically encoded and tunable architectural parameter of vertebrate mitochondria. In this model, SPRIZ is a molecular spacing system that locally sets OMM–IMM separation, shaping the environment through which metabolites, ions, and signals diffuse and establishing local gradients within the IMS.

title: The network structure of the urban revolution
abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. On average, 916 million people per year were exposed to at least one coexposure day, increasing by 287 million people per decade. The global annual average exposed days per person was 1.3 days, rising from 1.0 days in 2000–2009 to 1.7 days in 2010–2019. Coexposure person-days increased by 5.5 billion per decade, of which 70.5% was attributable to increasing coexposure intensity and 29.5% to population growth. Countries with a low human development index (HDI) experienced the highest coexposure days per person and the greatest increases. These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
abstract:
Klebsiella pneumoniae
                    is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children.
                    K. pneumoniae
                    isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from
                    K. pneumoniae
                    neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative
                    K. pneumoniae
                    vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of
                    K. pneumoniae.
                    Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal
                    K. pneumoniae
                    infection.

title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. In this work, we demonstrate a classical simulation outperforming Gaussian boson sampling experiments of 100 modes on established benchmark tests using a single central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). Being embarrassingly parallelizable, a small number of CPUs or GPUs allows us to match previous sampling rates that required more than 100 GPUs. We believe that algorithmic and implementation improvements have the potential to generalize our tools to photocounting and pseudo–photon number–resolving scenarios and larger system sizes. Last, most of the innovations in our tools remain valid for generic probability distributions over binary variables, rendering them potentially applicable to the simulation of qubit-based sampling problems and creating classical surrogates for classical-quantum algorithms.

title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO 2 release in alpine landscapes
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission–driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

abstract:

Combining thermal transport, low-temperature heat capacity, Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron x-ray pair distribution function analysis, and anharmonic lattice-dynamics calculations, we uncover the microscopic origin of this anomalous heat transport. Chemical bonding heterogeneity, weakly bound rattling-like Cs vibrations, anisotropic Cl dynamics, and soft lattice modes generate low-energy localized optical phonons that strongly interact with acoustic modes. Enhanced three- and four-phonon scattering suppresses phonon lifetimes, while anharmonic renormalization flattens optical branches and reduces group velocities. title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
abstract:
In most cells,
                    Malat1
                    long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons,
                    Malat1
                    is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

title: Layered superlattices: from physical assembly to chemical synthesis and emerging applications
abstract: This review summarizes the classification, physical and chemical synthesis, and structure–property relationships of layered superlattices, with emphasis on emerging applications, structural control, dynamic characterization, and device integration.

title: Graphite from Mars
An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
abstract:
Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C
                    −1
                    between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                    tic
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                    tic
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

title: High‐Performance Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers via a Tandem Alignment Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers have shown great potential as shape‐memory soft materials due to their large and reversible deformation capacity. However, fabrication methods for LCE fibers with ultrafast thermal response and the exploration of the factors influencing their thermal actuation performance remain limited. A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning is presented to fabricate highly aligned LCE fibers. These LCE fibers achieve an order parameter of up to 0.78 and exhibit exceptional actuation performance under thermal stimulation, including an actuation strain of 80%, an actuation speed of 1485% s −1 , and a peak power density of 6105 W kg −1 . Furthermore, the actuation performance can be significantly enhanced by resonance. Under constant heating conditions, modulation of the heating frequency enables the actuation speed of the LCE fibers to be amplified up to 10‐fold, achieving bioinspired energy efficiency optimization similar to the wing‐flapping of insects. The LCE fibers demonstrate promising applicability in scenarios requiring ultrafast and efficient thermal actuation.

title: Negative‐Thermal‐Expansion Strategy Enables Hard Carbon With Tuned Heat/Strain Tolerances for Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT The thermal/stress runaways pose a risk to the safety and industrialization of sodium‐ion battery (SIB), which hence requires external management equipment. Actually, the thermal/stress generation originates from the repetitive Na + intercalation within carbon interlayers and pore‐filling in the initial stage. Herein, we propose a regulation strategy of “in situ thermal strain relief” to achieve internal thermal and stress managements of SIB hard carbon (HC) anode by incorporating negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW 2 O 8 . The results indicate that the heat and strain were reduced obviously after cycling, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and enhanced sodium storage capacity. Moreover, the microstructure and efficient electron/ion transport within HC were preserved, demonstrating excellent capacity stability even after high‐rate and long‐term cycling over wide operating temperature ranges (−20°C to 60°C). This study provides a new approach for thermal and stress management inside the battery, which may play a joint effort with the conventional management equipment outside the battery and beyond.

title: Tuning N‐Species Adsorption/Desorption Equilibrium by Ni 1 Au n ‐SrTiO 3 for Artificial Urea Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Inefficient generation of N‐related intermediates, stemming from inert adsorption/photoactivation of N 2 , has hindered efficient artificial photosynthesis of urea from N 2 , CO 2 , and H 2 O. To overcome this bottleneck, we herein propose a strategy for modulating the adsorption/desorption equilibrium of N‐related species using precisely designed bimetallic Ni 1 Au n active sites supported on a strontium titanate (NiAu‐STO) semiconductor photocatalyst. This strategy significantly enhances N 2 adsorption/activation and effective generation of N‐related intermediates to facilitate C–N coupling for the photocatalytic urea synthesis, affording a considerable urea production rate of 1333.63 µg g cat. −1 , with successful crystallization of a collectible solid‐phase urea product. Furthermore, we developed a novel reaction‐temperature programmed desorption‐mass spectrometry tandem monitoring system to elucidate the adsorption behavior of N 2 , which can clarify the adsorption behavior of N 2 and confirm the formation of critical N‐related intermediates (e.g., *NH 2 ) on the NiAu‐STO photocatalyst. In addition, in situ Raman spectroscopy results further validated the formation of a distinctive C–N coupling intermediate (*NH 2 COO – ) on the photocatalyst surface, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis from N 2 , CO 2 , and H 2 O.

title: Polyacrylate‐Based Dielectric Elastomer Fiber Actuators for High‐Performance Artificial Muscles
abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric elastomer fiber actuators (DEFAs) are promising candidates for artificial muscle applications, owing to their high axial actuation and mechanical compliance, yet achieving scalable fabrication without compromising electromechanical performance remains a critical bottleneck. Existing continuous manufacturing routes are predominantly restricted to silicone elastomers, which yield limited actuation strains and low energy densities. Here, a continuous fabrication strategy that integrates coaxial wet spinning with in situ ultraviolet curing is developed to produce polyacrylate‐based DEFAs (PA‐DEFAs) from a bimodal‐networked polyacrylate dielectric elastomer at rates up to 22.5 mm s −1 . The fiber geometry and electromechanical properties are readily tunable by adjusting the core‐to‐shell flow‐rate ratio and elastomer formulation. The resulting fiber actuators deliver a maximum prestretch‐free axial strain of ∼39%, a maximum energy density of 54.8 J kg − 1 , and a peak power density of 443 W kg − 1 —outperforming previously reported continuously fabricated DEFAs. The long and continuous fiber architecture further enables wrapped actuator and parallel‐connected arrays, facilitating seamless integration into diverse soft robotic systems, including a robotic arm, a crawling robot, and an underwater robotic manta‐ray with modular fault‐tolerance. By reconciling scalable manufacturing with high actuation performance, PA‐DEFAs establish a versatile and manufacturing‐compatible platform for next‐generation artificial muscles and adaptive soft robotics.

title: Self‐Fueling Nanobacteria Harnesses Leaked Pancreatic Fluid to Eradicate Residual Tumors After Surgery
abstract: ABSTRACT Postoperative management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains hindered by two closely linked challenges: the harmful effects of pancreatic fistula and the high risk of local tumor recurrence. Although leaked pancreatic fluid (PF) is generally regarded as a postoperative complication, its abundance of digestive enzymes also suggests an underexplored therapeutic opportunity. Here, we developed a localized therapeutic strategy that converts the enzyme‐rich fistula microenvironment from a pathological burden into an antitumor resource. To achieve this, we nano‐engineered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B.t.) and integrated it with TRPV1 antagonist‐loaded nanomicelles in a GelMA hydrogel, generating the platform TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel. Mechanistically, this system acts in a coordinated manner within the postoperative PDAC microenvironment. B.t. degrades tumor‐associated mucins, thereby dismantling the protective barrier that shields PDAC cells from pancreatic enzymes and restoring their vulnerability to enzymatic attack. Meanwhile, PF forms an in situ digestive enzyme corona on the nanoengineered bacterial surface, which promotes deeper tumor penetration by disrupting intercellular adhesion. In parallel, delivery of the TRPV1 antagonist (TRPV1a) suppresses CGRP release, attenuates cancer‐associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, and facilitates NK‐cell‐associated antitumor responses. In postoperative PDAC models, TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel showed durable local retention, enhanced tumor accumulation, suppressed recurrence, prolonged survival, and alleviated pain‐related behaviors without evident systemic toxicity.

title: Redefining the thermal safety boundaries of ether-based sodium batteries
abstract: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.

title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: Limited impacts of methane pyrolysis for energy on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions
